# The protocol's vocabulary

One word for each concept the protocol's prose names. This page is generated from the terms registry, `tools/internal/terms/terms.json`. The same registry is what `manual` prints to each seat as WORDS THIS SURFACE USES, and what the vocabulary gate (`TestVocabularyProse`, in `tools/integration/surface`) holds every seat-facing surface to. Change the registry, then regenerate: `(cd scripts && go run ./vocabdoc)`.

A **GATED** variant fails the gate wherever it appears, unless a mask blanks it or an allow exempts its file. A **REGISTRY-ONLY** variant is defined here and not gated, because the word has a legitimate neighbour sense no exact phrase can tell apart. A **mask** is a legitimate phrase blanked before the pattern runs; an **allow** exempts a file, and says why.

## the report

The report is the research prose written for a reader of the subject: one document from a lane's text to what the run assembles at its end, named by its stage only where the stage matters — your part of the report, the report as `show report` serves it, which is the only way a seat reads it, and the copy assembled for the human reader once the run is over.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| candidate draft | GATED | `candidate drafts?\|drafts? candidates` |  |  |
| candidate (the text) | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |
| living report | GATED | `living report` |  |  |
| document or artifact under audit | GATED | `(document\|artifact) under audit` |  |  |
| synthesis (the document) | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |
| deliverable | GATED | `deliverables?` |  |  |
| blue/report.md | GATED | `blue/report\.md` |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **candidate** — a gap a lens is about to mint keeps the word; lane text is the report
- **report.md** — report.md at the run root is the assembled report; no seat writes blue/report.md

## run directory

The run directory is the directory that holds one run: its record, its report and the documents assembled beside it.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blackboard | GATED | `blackboard` |  |  |

## the record

The record is the run's account of every act, held as events in records/record.db, and every read a seat makes is a projection of it.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **record (verb)** — as a verb, say "put on the record" or name the verb that does it

## run

A run is one research question taken from setup to its outcome.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## epoch

An epoch runs from one chair sitting to the next: the chair relays who sits, the parties the record names sit, and the chair sits again.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| round | GATED | `\brounds?\b` | `round-trip` — a round-trip is a request and its answer, not a unit of the run |  |

## sitting

A sitting is one seat's dispatch, from the prompt the engine hands it to the envelope it returns.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| your last turn, your next turn | GATED | `your (last\|next) turn` |  |  |
| this session | GATED | `this session` |  |  |
| turn (a sitting) | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **turn** — a NULL TURN (a sitting that moved nothing on a gap) and an API turn (one model call inside a sitting) keep the word

## failed sitting

A failed sitting is a sitting of a seat whose work arrives as items that closed with no envelope admitted: the call returning its envelope never succeeded, because the envelope gate refused it or its schema rejected it until the harness gave up, or its agent died; the engine dispatches the seat again while it owes its items, and capture names each one.

**Delivered to:** operator

**Collisions:**

- **FAIL (a verdict)** — the chair's FAIL is a judgement on the board; a failed sitting is a sitting that ended without its envelope admitted, and judges nothing

## exchange

An exchange is blue's sitting on one gap followed by its minting lens's audit of the answer, and k-max counts them.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## seat

A seat is one agent's place in the run, registered under a seat id whose role decides the surface it is given.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## side

A side is red or blue: red audits the report and passes or fails it, blue researches, writes and repairs it.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| red team, blue team | GATED | `(blue\|red) teams?` | `## Blue team report` — quotes a wrapper heading blue must not write; the prompt names the forbidden form, not a side |  |

## lens

A lens is a red seat that audits the report for one class of defect, and the only seat that files findings and mints gaps.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **method** — a lane's source method is its method, never a lens

## chair

The chair is red's running seat: it relays who sits, rules blue's motions, spot-checks the stale areas before a PASS and records red's verdict.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **merge** — blue's union of the lanes' parts is a merge; the chair is the chair

## bench

The bench is the seat that adjudicates the contested docket, rules on motions and stamps how the run ended.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

|---|---|---|---|---|
| the judge | GATED | `the judge([^a-z]\|$)` |  |  |

- **stopping judgment** — the chair's is PASS when the board permits it; the bench's is whether remaining defect is worth remaining cost

## lane

A lane is one of blue's parallel first passes at the report, written by one researcher under one method.

**Delivered to:** blue, lane, bench, operator

## synthesizer

The synthesizer is the blue seat that merges the lanes' parts into the report by union through the record's acts, and writes the report's authored surfaces.

**Delivered to:** blue, lane, bench, operator

## engine

The engine is the workflow script that dispatches the seats the record says are ready and reads the envelopes they return.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the lead | GATED | `the lead([^a-z]\|$)` |  |  |
| harness (the engine) | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **harness** — the Claude Code runtime a seat runs inside keeps the word

## lead session

A run's lead session is the Claude Code session its live-run row names — the one that ran setup, or took the run over since — and the hooks attribute an agent to the run only when its payload's session_id is that session.

**Delivered to:** operator

**Collisions:**

- **the lead** — "the lead" alone is the engine's banned variant; a session that leads a run is "the run's lead session", never "the lead"

## operator

The operator is the person running the research, and the seat id their own commands run under.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## the log

The log is the entries a seat files for the operator with the `log` verb — a missing capability, a defect in the tooling, or friction, never a clean sitting, which is derived from having sat and filed no log entry — and none of it is debate material.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| operator channel | GATED | `operator('s)? channel` |  |  |
| friction verb | GATED | `friction verb` |  |  |
| complaint channel | GATED | `complaint channel` |  |  |
| the envelope's friction field | GATED | `envelope's .friction. field` |  |  |
| friction (the whole log) | GATED | `\blog is (open — )?for friction\b\|\bmet no friction\b\|\bfriction (channel\|log\|footer)\b\|\blog \([^)]*\) — friction\b\|\b(collated\|collected\|aggregated\|gathered) friction\b\|\bfriction (so far\|collected\|collated\|aggregated\|gathered)\b\|\bthe (run\|sitting\|seat\|bench\|chair)'s friction\b` |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **log** — `log` only ever writes; the operator reads the log with `ops log`

## friction

Friction is one type of log entry: something cost the seat a call, a guess or an act — a refusal, a guessed name, a misread shape, a workaround — and it notes what it expected and why, whether or not anything should change; an act no surface offers at all is a request, not friction.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| impeded / impediment (the log read as blockage) | GATED | `\bimped(e\|ed\|es\|ing\|iment\|iments)\b` |  |  |

## missing capability

A missing capability is an act a seat needed that no surface offers, and it goes in the log, never on the board.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## citation

A citation is a source attached to a sentence of the report with the cite verb, hashed and dated so it can be checked again.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| source note | GATED | `source notes?` |  |  |
| reference (a citation) | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **reference** — references/*.md and the proto's references option keep the word

## source span

A source span is the words a citation quotes from the source's own cached text, which the tool finds there once and keeps on the citation with the source's text around them; it is what the source says, and blue's reason for the citation is blue's account of it.

**Delivered to:** lens, blue, lane

## source search

A source search is a read of one cached source's text for a pattern, in the text and the normalisation a source span is located in; each hit carries the source's sentence around it and whether a citation can quote that sentence as printed, and the search records nothing.

**Delivered to:** lens, blue, lane

## OCR-derived text

OCR-derived text is a machine's reading of a scanned document's page images: deterministic, and able to misread, so a citation quoting it records the PDF page its quote sits on and is checked against that page's image.

**Delivered to:** lens, blue, lane, operator

## anchor

An anchor is the invisible token a citation, a computation, a finding or a gap leaves at its sentence in the report.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## computation

A computation is a program blue ran and recorded as evidence: its bundle, stored by its sha256, with the output and exit status of its run, and a basis — `reproducible` when two runs wrote the same bytes, `variant` when they differed and blue stated what holds across them.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## finding anchor

A finding anchor is the anchor a lens's finding leaves at the sentence the finding is about.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| finding-marker, marker layer | GATED | `finding markers?\|marker layer` |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **marker** — the `.run-live` marker and the manual's `→ SHARED` marker keep the word

## verdict

The verdict is the chair's PASS or FAIL on the board.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

## outcome

The outcome is how the run ended: VERIFIED, CEILING, HALTED or UNVERIFIED.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## finding

A finding is a lens's recorded observation of a defect in the report, or of a dispute with a gap already on the board, graded and not yet minted.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| finding (a complaint about the tooling) | GATED | `\bfinding about the tooling\b` |  |  |
| finding (a capture-audit failure) | GATED | `\bfinding against you\b` |  |  |

## gap

A gap is a defect in the report that changes a conclusion or a decision a reader makes, minted onto the board by a lens.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **gap** — a parity gap between two numbers is ordinary English; a missing tool is a missing capability

## material

A gap is material when its class is always material, or when its class goes by grade and its current severity is medium or above, and an open material gap holds the PASS gate.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **material** — material as content, or as bearing on the reader's question, is ordinary English; a gap is material only by its class and grade

## blocker

A blocker is one entry on the list the verdict gate refuses a PASS on, with the seat whose act clears it.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, bench

**Collisions:**

- **blocking (a work item)** — `show work` marks an item blocking when the seat's sitting is not complete while it is open, and such an item is a blocker only when the verdict gate's list carries it

## contradiction

A contradiction is a source red read that refutes, or is silent on, a claim of the report, raised by the finding that names its id (a reading of that claim after the raise opens a new contradiction with its own id), and held open until the gap minted from that finding answers it, or until blue retires the citation it was read against, or that citation is checked against its sentence as it now stands and backed by every lens's latest check of it; the finding alone answers nothing, and a contradiction is not a report contradicting itself, which is the defect class `cross_section_contradiction`, anchored by quote.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair

**Collisions:**

- **contradiction (ordinary English)** — a text at odds with itself, such as a report contradicting itself or a stamp that says the opposite of the board, keeps the ordinary word; the record's contradiction is the reading red recorded, whether its outcome is `refutes` or `absent`

## retire

To retire a claim is to take it out of the report with the retire verb, on the record; retiring a citation alone takes its anchor out of the report and keeps the sentence it stood on word for word.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| claims withdrawn | GATED | `claims? withdrawn` |  |  |
| withdraw (retire) | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **retired (a lens)** — a lens retires from dispatch, which is a state of the seat; a claim is retired from the report, on the record

## lens retirement

Lens retirement is the record's state for a lens that has stopped finding material: three sittings in a row it sat through without a fresh material gap retire a lens that owes nothing on its work list — nothing new on a gap it minted since it last sat, no contradiction it read, no check it owns, no gap owed about a check of its that failed — and a head move does not ready a retired lens; a sitting stopped at the per-sitting call limit, or one that never closed, is not one it sat through and counts neither way.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, operator

## stale area

A stale area is the area of a retired lens whose pin is behind the report head, which the chair reads and names in a spot-check before a PASS.

**Delivered to:** chair, operator

## report read

A report read is the record's evidence that the tool served a lens the whole report at a head, written by the report's whole read and by no read at an anchor or a selection; it says the text was served, not that it was read, and the head of a lens's latest one in a sitting it sat through is its pin, which the lens is readied past.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, operator

**Collisions:**

- **pin (a dispatch's)** — a dispatch's pin is the head the chair engages a party at; a lens's pin is the head of its latest report read in a sitting it sat through, and the lens is ready while the report head is past it

## disposition

A disposition is the bench's ruling value on a docketed gap, and it decides whether the gap closes.

| carry (a remand) | GATED | `\b(gaps?\|dockets?) (that )?(you\|the bench) (can )?carr(y\|ies\|ied\|ying)\b\|\bcarr(y\|ies\|ied\|ying) (the gaps?\|a gap\|gaps\|the dockets?)\b\|\b(by\|you\|the bench\|or\|may\|can\|must) carr(y\|ies\|ied\|ying) (it\|them)\b\|\bcarried (gaps?\|dockets?)\b\|\bcarr(y\|ies\|ied\|ying)\b[^.]{0,60}\bdeadlock` |  |  |

## grade movement

Grade movement is the change a lens's regrade makes to a gap's severity, likelihood or impact, weighed as the difference in mass between the two grades in either direction, and once the open gaps' movement no docket ruling on its gap has followed totals more than 2.0 the dispatch dockets each such gap for the bench and a PASS waits for its ruling; the bench's own regrade is the grade its ruling sets and is no movement.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **movement (an exchange's)** — an exchange moves its gap when the gap's grade, its anchored text or its lineage changes, blue answers it with a computation or a fate on its inquiry, or it closes, which is what impasse counts; grade movement is the regrade part of that alone, weighed in mass

## grade motion

A grade motion is a motion contesting a gap's grade, filed by any seat but the chair, which rules it.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| grade dispute | GATED | `grade disputes?` |  |  |
| grade_disputes (the envelope key) | GATED | `grade_disputes` |  |  |

## relief

Relief is the order the bench records when it grants a petition: what the seats it binds must or must not do, with whom it binds, carried from the ruling to every seat's work list.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Collisions:**

- **relief sought** — the petitioner's ask, on the filing; relief is what the bench ordered on the ruling

## new grounds

New grounds are what a docket motion on a gap the bench ruled closed names to be admitted: an act recorded after the ruling and about the gap, located by its id or by a quote of report text an edit answering the gap wrote since, which the tool checks.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## scorecard

A scorecard is the numbers a seat is measured on, computed from the record: red's for the lenses and the chair, blue's for blue's seats, the bench's for the bench.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| your chair (a scorecard) | GATED | `your chair` |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **card** — a card is one of the three scorecards, red, blue or bench, and nothing else

## occasion

A sitting's occasion is what it was convened to do — the question put to the seat, as against the seat id, which says who was asked — and only the bench carries one, because its five sittings share a single id.

**Delivered to:** bench

**Not:**

| variant | kind | pattern | masks | allowed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sitting kind | GATED | `sitting kinds?\b` |  |  |
| sitting type | GATED | `sitting types?\b` |  |  |
| bench mode | REGISTRY-ONLY |  |  |  |

**Collisions:**

- **occasion (ordinary English)** — "for want of occasion" in a log entry is the plain word and keeps it; the FIELD is the one a bench register carries

## inquiry

An inquiry is one question the research could take up — proposed by blue with the hypothesis that would be true if it paid off, recorded with what became of it, open to a ruling by the chair, and reviewed against the report once per epoch.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator

## reopened

A citation or computation is reopened when an edit changes its sentence after a check and no sitting opened since has checked it — it is unchecked again; its owning lens owes the check and is the seat readied for it — the evidence lens for a citation, the lens that owns computations for a computation — a check by any lens from a sitting opened after the edit clears it, and a PASS waits until one does.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, operator

**Collisions:**

- **reopen (a gap)** — minting a successor over a closed gap reopens the gap, and a ruling's `reopens_on` says what would: neither is a reopened citation or computation
- **`reopened` (the edit's field)** — an edit's `reopened` lists every anchor its sentence change touched, of any kind, and `show work`'s `edited_since` reads it; only a citation or computation among them, checked before the edit, is reopened

## unchecked

A citation or computation is unchecked when no check of the sentence the report carries stands: nobody has checked it, or it is reopened; its owning lens owes the check and is readied for it, and a PASS waits until one is recorded.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, operator

## failed check

A failed check is a standing check of a citation or computation that failed — a lens judged the computation's sentence unsound, or every reading of the citation since its sentence last changed read nothing of the cited work, the source unreachable or the copy not the work — which holds the PASS, is cleared by no bench ruling, and obliges the seat whose check failed to mint a gap about the anchor, outside its mint budget, that does not close while the check stands, until the anchor is checked and holds, an edit changes its sentence, or blue retires it.

**Delivered to:** lens, chair, blue, lane, bench, operator
